Subject: Priv deploy: operator access & retention clarifications

Hi Connor / Laura,

Thanks again for the demo last week — VitalCare is excited to move the Private VPC pilot forward. Before our procurement team drafts PO language, a couple of open items from compliance that I need clarified (so the procurement folks can model the risk and acceptance):

- Operator access model: you have previously described a "stewarded operator" model where Redwood personnel may perform snapshot validation in a customer VPC. We need the exact checklist you use during that process and how access is limited (session duration, MFA, IP allowlist, console vs. agent-based access).
- License scope for on-prem: does the Order Form + private-deploy addendum carve out model residency or grant a limited-use license for snapshots/runbooks to be executed by the customer? Procurement wants clear language they can include in the SOW.
- Evidence & escrow-like asks: our security team may request a signed statement or snapshots for continuity — what form factors do you support (signed witness, encrypted image, escrowed artifacts, attestation letters)? Also, what is the proposed retention and deletion workflow for those artifacts?

Attached: VitalCare-SOW.pdf (draft). Can you point me to the evidence checklist and share any runbook excerpt that describes the operator validation steps? We can set a short call if helpful — procurement would like to resolve the acceptance criteria this week.

Best,
Aditi Sharma
Sr. Program Manager, Integrations
VitalCare AI

Hi Aditi — thanks for the clear list. Quick responses and next steps below: 

1) Operator access / validation checklist: we have a short runbook excerpt that covers (a) temporary console access via short-lived credentials, (b) session recording retention policy, (c) MFA and IP restriction requirements, and (d) least-privilege roles scoped to snapshot/validation operations only. I'll attach the runbook digest and a one-page checklist.
2) License scope: our standard private-deploy addendum grants Redwood a narrowly-scoped, non-commercial right to instantiate model snapshots solely for validation and failover testing; it does not grant broader distribution rights. Laura is looping in legal for precise suggested MSA language.
3) Evidence / escrow: we support encrypted snapshot transfer under an NDA, and we can provide a signed attestation of access and validation steps. We do not currently offer third-party escrow custody by default, but we can propose an "escrow-lite" workflow (encrypted snapshot + notarized attestation + time-limited access token) for customers who require it.

If it helps, I propose a 30-min working session Thursday (6/5) to walk procurement through the checklist and proposed addendum text. Same time we can drop the runbook fragment into a shared Drive.

Connor

Aditi / Connor — looping in a few legal and delivery points. I reviewed the SOW draft and summarized our asks and proposed MSA redline positions below. I've attached a first-pass redline for the private-deploy addendum.

Key items we'd like to confirm (short list):
- Explicit license boundary: order form + addendum should state that Redwood retains model IP and that any snapshots transferred to the customer are licensed for internal run/test and continuity purposes only; no redistribution. Suggested clause in redline: "Customer is granted a non-exclusive, revocable, limited license to use delivered snapshots solely for internal continuity and testing; all other rights reserved."
- Operator proof: we can provide signed attestations and session recordings as evidence of operator activity. Customer requests for raw snapshot images require a documented evidence request and an agreed acceptance test. We propose an approval window (30 days) for the customer to review evidence following delivery.
- Escrow-lite workflow: addendum includes option (A) encrypted snapshot + RSA-signed attestation delivered to customer, or (B) encrypted snapshot deposited with mutually-agreed custodian (third party) for the duration of the agreement. Custodian option requires explicit fees and SLA.
- Retention & deletion: define retention periods for session recordings and evidence artifacts (e.g., 90 days for session logs, 365 days for escrowed artifacts unless renewal).

Action items for VitalCare / MedSys procurement: please confirm whether you expect raw snapshot handover or if a signed attestation + test workload run is sufficient. That choice will affect both license language and delivery timelines.

Attachment: MedSys-MSA-Redlines_v1.pdf (application/pdf, stub)

Thanks,
Laura Bennett
Senior Counsel, Redwood Inference
laura.bennett@redwoodinference.com
